content:
Benji Okafor: quick bikeshed before we lock telemetry for guardrails gating. need naming conventions for metrics + labels, and hard rules on cardinality. can we align here so i don’t have to redo the schema PR?

Jordan Lee: +1. Also want to be explicit on what ends up as a metric label vs what stays in audit logs / traces.

Ethan Park: constraints from control plane side: we need enough breakdown to answer “why did this apply block?” but we can’t explode prom cardinality w/ tenant+route+model_version+promptset.

Logan Wright: yup. rule of thumb: any ID-like thing (tenant_id, route_id, eval_run_id) is a no-go label. if it’s unbounded, keep it out of metrics.

Allison Grant: +1. also please follow prom naming conventions. if we’re emitting to prometheus, metric names should be `snake_case`, units in name, counters end in `_total`, histograms w/ `_bucket/_sum/_count`.

Benji Okafor: ok so don’t use the dot-style `redwood.optimize.guardrails.*`? i see both styles across services.

Allison Grant: dots are fine in logs, but for prometheus metric name itself: prefer `redwood_optimize_guardrails_*`. (we can keep `service.name=redwood.optimize.guardrails` as a resource attr if otel)

Caleb Johnson: fwiw our otel->prom bridge already replaces dots in `meter` names, but it’s messy. would rather be consistent and not rely on rewriting.

Jordan Lee: can we define a “core set” of metrics for gating:
- decision outcomes (pass/fail/timeout/error)
- eval latency
- runner queue depth/backlog
- override usage
- suite selection counts

Logan Wright: yes. suggested metric list (names tentative):
- `redwood_optimize_guardrails_decisions_total{outcome=pass|fail|timeout|error, enforcement=observe_only|soft_block|hard_block}`
- `redwood_optimize_guardrails_eval_latency_seconds` (histogram)
- `redwood_optimize_guardrails_eval_jobs_inflight` (gauge)
- `redwood_optimize_guardrails_eval_queue_depth` (gauge)
- `redwood_optimize_guardrails_overrides_total{result=approved|denied|canceled}`

Nadia Rahman: for cost attribution we also need to correlate config changes w/ “expected savings” buckets. but pls don’t add a label w/ numeric savings. we can do a coarse bucket label like `savings_bucket=lt5|5_15|15_30|gt30` (%).

Ethan Park: what about `optimization_type` label? we’ll want split by quantization vs batching vs caching vs routing.

Logan Wright: bounded enum → ok as label.

Allison Grant: label names should be consistent too. please no camelCase. also avoid `type` as label name (too generic). use `optimization` or `optimization_type`.

Benji Okafor: label list i’m thinking:
- `optimization_type` (quantization|batching|caching|routing)
- `workload_type` (chat|embeddings|rerank|tool_calling|structured)
- `model_family` (llama|mistral|qwen|mixtral|other)
- `customer_tier` (free|pro|enterprise|internal)
- `region` (us-east-1|eu-west-1|…)
- `enforcement_stage` (observe_only|soft_block|hard_block)
- `failure_reason` (?)

Jordan Lee: `failure_reason` is where we’ll get wrecked. if it’s free-form string from policy engine it will explode.

Logan Wright: strongly recommend failure_reason be a bounded enum. like 10-20 max. e.g. `metric_regression`, `min_sample_size_not_met`, `ci_overlap`, `eval_runner_timeout`, `suite_config_error`, `policy_config_missing`, `artifact_store_error`, `internal_error`.

Ethan Park: from policy engine we also have per-metric failure (“factuality_delta_exceeded”, “format_compliance_drop”). that’s going to be a ton.

Allison Grant: per-metric granularity belongs in the gating result payload (audit log) and maybe tracing attributes on the span, not as a prometheus label.

Caleb Johnson: if we do want *some* per-metric view, we could do a separate metric with a very small controlled set of “top-level metrics” only. but if someone later adds 40 metrics, cardinality creeps.

Logan Wright: +1. we can have:
`redwood_optimize_guardrails_failed_metric_total{metric=factuality|format|toxicity|task_success}`
where `metric` is *category*, not the raw metric id.

Jordan Lee: yes, metric taxonomy category label is safer. raw metric ids should stay in artifacts.

Benji Okafor: ok so no `metric_name=exact_metric_id` label. categories only.

Nadia Rahman: also please avoid `model_version` label. that’s basically infinite.

Benji Okafor: i was going to add `model` label (like `llama-3.1-70b-instruct@2024-12-05`). guess not.

Allison Grant: do not.

Ethan Park: what can we do instead for model? we still need to answer “is llama family failing more after new thresholds?”

Logan Wright: `model_family` + `deployment_mode` (hosted|dedicated|private) should cover most dashboards. for deeper drilldown we rely on logs/traces (and the Console can filter via backend queries).

Felix Schneider: from Console side, we can link “view details” to a stored gating_run_id and show exact model version/prompt set there. we don’t need that in metrics.

Jordan Lee: also label `prompt_set_rev` is a no. too many.

Benji Okafor: got it. so where do prompt_set_rev / threshold_version go?

Jordan Lee: audit event payload + eval run summary object. store as fields. then you can slice in analytics warehouse if needed.

Caleb Johnson: traces can carry `threshold_version` as span attr, but don’t send it to prom via exemplars unless we’re sure it’s bounded. versions change every time.

Allison Grant: exactly. even `threshold_version` could be high churn, even if bounded at any given time. for prom, prefer `policy_track=pilot|ga` or `policy_profile=default|quant_strict` etc.

Logan Wright: recommendation:
- metrics labels: only stable enums
- logs/audit: ids + full detail
- traces: ids for correlation (ok), sampled

Ethan Park: +1. also “tenant_id”: NO. but can we do `tenant_tier` yes.

Benji Okafor: what about `tenant_slug` for internal testing?

Allison Grant: no. even internal tenants become unbounded eventually. use `customer_tier=internal` + a separate debug-only log query.

Jordan Lee: also: please keep label names consistent across metrics. e.g. use `customer_tier` everywhere, not sometimes `tier`.

Nadia Rahman: one more: for latency histogram, can we add `optimization_type` and `outcome`? outcome on latency could be useful (timeouts vs passes).

Logan Wright: `optimization_type` ok. `outcome` ok. but do not add `workload_type` to latency histogram unless we’re sure it’s small. (it is small, but still adds series). might be fine.

Allison Grant: latency histograms already multiply series by bucket count. keep labels minimal. I’d do only `outcome` + maybe `enforcement_stage`. Anything else → derive via logs.

Caleb Johnson: +1. histograms with 4 labels turn into a lot fast.

Benji Okafor: ok final proposal, pls react :thumbsup: / :no_entry:.

Benji Okafor: Metric naming:
- `redwood_optimize_guardrails_decisions_total`
- `redwood_optimize_guardrails_overrides_total`
- `redwood_optimize_guardrails_eval_latency_seconds` (hist)
- `redwood_optimize_guardrails_eval_queue_depth` (gauge)
- `redwood_optimize_guardrails_eval_jobs_inflight` (gauge)
- `redwood_optimize_guardrails_failed_metric_total` (optional, taxonomy category only)

Benji Okafor: Label rules:
- allowed labels (bounded enums): `outcome`, `enforcement_stage`, `optimization_type`, `customer_tier`, `model_family`, `deployment_mode`, `region`, `failure_reason` (enum only), `metric_category` (enum only)
- banned labels: `tenant_id`, `tenant_slug`, `route_id`, `model_version`, `prompt_set_rev`, `eval_run_id`, anything numeric/unbounded

Ethan Park: :thumbsup: looks good. i’d like `deployment_mode` included for sure.

Logan Wright: :thumbsup: +1. and please document the enum list for `failure_reason` in the repo so nobody “just adds a new string”.

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: works. add a lint/checklist in PR template if possible.

Caleb Johnson: :thumbsup: from ingestion side this is sane.

Nadia Rahman: :thumbsup: ok. for cost correlation we’ll use warehouse joins.

Jordan Lee: :thumbsup: agree. will update policy engine to output the top-level failure_reason enum + put detailed per-metric failures only in the gating result payload.

Benji Okafor: cool. i’ll update schema + telemetry spec accordingly and link this thread in the PR. thanks all.
